title: Unleashing the Potential of PIM: Accelerating Large Batched Inference of Transformer-Based Generative Models
problem: Transformer inference bottlenecks at attention computation where KV matrices exhibit low compute-to-bandwidth ratio regardless of batch size, and KV matrix aggregate size can exceed model weights, making conventional GPUs inefficient for this workload.
motivation: Batched transformer inference with longer sequences requires efficient attention computation to maintain serving throughput as sequence length grows.
method: AttAcc uses multiple processing-in-memory devices that exploit the write-once-read-many pattern of KV matrices. Each PIM device performs matrix-vector multiplication locally between embedding vectors and its portion of KV matrices, eliminating repeated inter-device bandwidth requirements while keeping computations localized to memory.
key_novelty: Exploiting the write-once-read-many access pattern of KV matrices by performing all multiplication operations within distributed PIM devices to reduce external bandwidth by orders of magnitude.
contributions: Identifies attention as the critical bottleneck in batched transformer inference due to low operational intensity and massive KV matrix sizes
Proposes AttAcc architecture with multiple PIM devices for localized in-memory attention computation
Demonstrates potential for orders-of-magnitude bandwidth reduction through data-local processing
